title: E2E latency fairness region allocator with adaptive penalty bands
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Current region selection favors lowest recent p50 but can oscillate and overload nearby POPs when p95 spikes or path degradation occurs. Goal: implement an allocator that balances fairness (avoids starving regions), honors latency SLOs across p50/p95 percentiles, and incorporates a composite network-health penalty band that increases when loss/jitter/packet reordering or control-plane anomalies are observed.

Scope:
- Compute per-POP rolling p50 and p95 latency windows (1m/10m), normalized per model tier.
- Combine latency percentiles with network health score (0-100) into a single cost metric using configurable weights.
- Add adaptive penalty bands: small transient p95 blips incur soft penalties; sustained degradation escalates penalty tiers and triggers variant fallbacks or region drain.
- Integrate tier-awareness: premium customers route preferentially but can be steered when region cost > threshold.
- Provide operator knobs in Console: weights, penalty thresholds, decay half-life, and emergency global cap.

Acceptance criteria:
- New allocator reduces p95 tail impact on global error-rate by >= 30% in canary traffic.
- No increase in median latency > 5% for steady workloads.
- Console shows per-route cost decomposition (p50, p95, net-health, penalty).
- Automated fallback to compatible model variant happens within 10s of penalty escalation in canary.

Out-of-scope for initial roll: modelling of inter-POP bandwidth contention and active load-shedding on request ingress.

Related artifacts:
- Design spec: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/smart-routing/e2e-latency-fairness (internal)
- Perf benchmark PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1743
- Canary dashboard (grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/regions/e2e-allocator-canary
comments: 2025-01-28 - Marco Silva: Kickoff meeting notes attached to design doc. Agreed to use 1m/10m windows for p50/p95 and to ship a low-risk soft-penalty first iteration.
2025-02-03 - Claire Nguyen (PM): Added customer story for premium tiers — ensure a toggle so sales can disable aggressive steering for enterprise customers during trials.

2025-02-10 - Aisha Patel: Prototype cost function implemented in staging. Initial formula: cost = w1 * norm(p95) + w2 * norm(p50) + w3 * (100 - net_health) + penalty_band. Observed oscillation in weight set {0.6,0.3,0.1}; moving to {0.5,0.2,0.3} improved stability.

2025-02-17 - Marco Silva: Load-testing notes: under synthetic spike there was a 12s delay before penalty escalator moved region to tier-2 penalty. Need to tune hysteresis/decay to avoid oscillation. Filed follow-up ENG-999001 for penalty algorithm tuning.

2025-02-21 - Security (Ethan Brooks): Security review required for telemetry aggregation pipeline; queries below 10s window must be rate-limited. Marked security_review_required = true; cleared on 2025-02-27 with minimal changes.

2025-02-27 - Marco Silva: Integrated KV cache hints so allocator knows hot-model sequence lengths; avoids misattributing high latency to region when it's model-context related. Patch: runtime PR #1743 referenced above.
2025-03-01 - Design (Priya Rao): Console UX wireframes uploaded to Drive; added 'Cost decomposition' tooltip and per-route override toggle. Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/design/console/allocator-ux

2025-03-04 - QA (Diego Martinez): Canary run (10% traffic) showed 32% reduction in tail-induced retries; telemetry shows no regression in p50. Found an edge-case: if two POPs alternate with identical cost, we occasionally bounce — added deterministic tie-breaker by POP stable-score (ENG-999120).
2025-03-06 - Marco Silva: In-progress tasks: finalize penalty escalation thresholds, add integration test for fallback-to-variant, implement Console knobs, and schedule canary ramp to 25% next week.
